patch_resolves_note: The staged patch.diff still does not apply to the reproduced workspace, but the authoritative `n132/arvo:30482-fix` image (RELIC commit `c76f09859ceea718c2d49ac4c6d9a9eeb13d04a9`) runs the original PoC clean and genuinely executes the same watched `bn_add(a1, a1, a0)` chain. On that fixed run `a1_alloc=68` and `a1_used=41`, and the watched top digit is fully initialized (`top_digit_init_prefix_len=8`) at both the grow site and the `bn_trim` sink.
verification_limitations: The helper `compile-target` fallback on the vulnerable image was not idempotent once `/src/relic/build` already existed, so Stage 04 rebuilt the instrumented target manually with the project's own component steps (`/src/relic/build`, `modules/relic`, then `cryptofuzz`) and the stock sanitizer flags before re-running the PoC.
Fixed-side source validation relied on the authoritative `30482-fix` image because the metadata `patch.diff` targets a later refactor and was rejected by the staged vulnerable snapshot.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

nodes.description: First exact RELIC-side statement on the crashing path that consumes attacker-controlled operand sizes and materializes the Karatsuba split size used to derive the vulnerable temporary lengths.

The high-half temporary `a1` is allocated at the build's default precision instead of the actual split length `a->used - h`. `bn_init()` does not zero the digit buffer, so any later growth of `a1` exposes unwritten tail digits.
MSan sink. `bn_trim()` reads the top digit of the addition result while trimming it, and on the witness that digit is uninitialized data propagated from the under-sized `a1` temporary.
Inside the watched `bn_add(a1, a1, a0)` call, `bn_grow(c, max)` leaves the newly materialized top digit slot of the grown result buffer uninitialized on the vulnerable execution.
nodes.evidence: The vulnerable trace records `grow_top_digit_state.top_digit_bytes=8` and `grow_top_digit_state.top_digit_init_prefix_len=0` immediately after `bn_grow(c, max)`.

nodes.description: The final remainder-copy iteration in `bn_add1_low()` reads and writes the same watched top-digit slot, so the grown tail digit is copied through unchanged to the result state consumed by `bn_trim()`.
nodes.evidence: The vulnerable trace records `tail_copy_top_digit.tail_src_ptr == tail_copy_top_digit.tail_dst_ptr == 0x7170000012c0`, proving the line-51 remainder copy operated on the same watched top-digit slot.

edges.description: The same temporary object `a1` allocated in `bn_mul_karat_imp` is the `c` result object that `bn_add_imp` grows inside the watched `bn_add(a1, a1, a0)` call.
The high-half logical length recorded in `a1->used` is passed unchanged as the `max` growth request inside the watched `bn_add_imp` call.
The watched top digit slot created by `bn_grow()` is the same source slot consumed by the final line-51 remainder copy in `bn_add1_low()`.
The watched top digit slot written by the final remainder-copy iteration is the same slot that `bn_trim()` later reads as `a->dp[a->used - 1]`.
